deviations: Only Volumetric Shadows Enabled changed from the all-on return baseline.
The counterfactual preceded its return baseline in the run order.
Additional rejected attempts extended the warm state before the accepted pass.

reasons: CSX used Info logging and a completed disk cache without compilation overlapping samples.
The scene and time reset were verified after the settle barrier.
All 38 retained frames were unique, resolved, newer than the arming boundary, and reported zero slot refusals.
Exact settings, raw profiler output, cache identity, runtime, scene, and hardware are retained.

conclusions: The Volumetric-Shadows-off GPU average was 5.2722 ms versus 5.2335 ms for the matched all-on return, an apparent +0.0387 ms rather than a saving.
The direction conflicts with the removed 0.0338 ms of directly timed shadow compute and is explained more plausibly by unrelated run variation, including a +0.0872 ms Upscaling difference.
The 0.0387 ms top-level difference is smaller than the 0.1392 ms all-on run-to-run drift, so this pass does not resolve the feature's marginal total cost.
The directly instrumented Volumetric Shadows compute cost remains usable as a component observation, not as the complete feature cost.
notes: Preparatory r01 and r02 artifacts are retained externally but rejected for pre-settle scene evidence and a retained pre-arm resolved frame respectively.
The settings-only MO2 override and its 3616-file cache lane remain available for switching without a full recompile.
No ShaderCache overlay files were generated; the setting-specific manifest matches the all-on Info cache superset.
